methodologySummary: A RateReveal reference range is a proprietary, market-informed pricing reference synthesized from documented external observations, payment-cost context, and explicit RateReveal product judgment. External sources inform the range but do not purport to publish or mathematically generate its exact boundaries. Qualification remains fail-closed to an approved segment, risk, channel, volume, processor, market, and statement period tuple.

researchBasis.summary: The approved evidence pack reviews fifteen business segments and eight modifier dimensions. The source records below preserve only the observations used by the five launch references, including metric type, quality, quantitative context, caveats, and direct locators; the remaining research is an expansion backlog, not production coverage.
limitations: No segment has a disclosed-methodology statistical distribution of actual merchant effective rates at the selected annual-volume tier.
Interchange schedules and processor pricing context inform cost reasoning but are not presented as observed all-in merchant effective-rate distributions.

sourceRecords.title: Average Credit Card Processing Fees and Costs in America
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: Card-present and card-not-present weighted-average processing-cost discussion
sourceRecords.metricType: interchange-plus weighted average and interchange context
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Reports card-present weighted-average context around 1.79% plus $0.08 and card-not-present context around 2.31% plus $0.25, with premium-card costs higher.
limitations: This is a compilation citing other data, not a primary statistical merchant study or a segment-and-volume-specific distribution.

sourceRecords.title: What Restaurants, Retailers, and Healthcare Practices Are Paying — Rates by Industry
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: States that restaurants typically see a 1.8%–2.4% effective rate and illustrates a roughly 2.9% flat-rate result on a $35 ticket.
limitations: Commercial payments provider with no disclosed sampling methodology; the observation is context, not an independent market distribution.

sourceRecords.title: The Complete Guide to Restaurant Credit Card Processing
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes interchange-plus restaurant pricing starting around 1.9% for $10-plus tickets and flat-rate pricing around 2.65%–2.75% for smaller-ticket contexts.
limitations: The page did not expose a stable publication date, and a starting price is a best-case floor rather than a typical merchant result.

sourceRecords.title: Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: Supermarket and regulated/exempt debit interchange tables
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Documents supermarket and debit interchange cost inputs, including regulated debit at 0.05% plus a fixed amount, that help explain grocery cost structure.
limitations: Interchange is only one component of merchant cost and does not establish an all-in merchant effective-rate range; specialty-food MCC qualification can differ.

sourceRecords.title: Regulation II — Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: 2024 covered, exempt, and blended debit interchange averages
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Reports covered debit averaging about 0.47%, exempt debit about 1.21%, and all debit about 0.73%, supporting debit-mix sensitivity in grocery pricing.
limitations: The data is not grocery-specific and the page identifies a data year rather than a discrete publication date.

sourceRecords.title: Data Brief: Grocery Customers Favor Debit Cards
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: A survey of 2,879 U.S. card users reports debit at 42% and credit at 32% of grocery transactions, supporting the importance of debit mix.
limitations: The survey is dated, self-reported rather than transaction-level, and does not directly measure processing cost.

sourceRecords.title: Credit Card Processing Fees: A 2026 Guide for Businesses
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes a broad 1.5%–3.5% processing-fee range and provides named processor examples for in-person and online pricing.
limitations: The range is broad and not a card-present, risk, or annual-volume-specific statistical distribution.

sourceRecords.title: How Much Are Payment Processing Fees in the USA in 2025?
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: Small-business and volume-tier all-in cost discussion
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes typical small-business all-in cost around 2.5%–3.5% and under-$1M merchants around 3.2%–4.0% after miscellaneous fees.
limitations: Processor-authored content with no disclosed dataset; the under-$1M tier is wider than RateReveal's selected volume tuple.

sourceRecords.title: The True Cost of Credit Card Processing in 2026: A Merchant's Guide
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes in-person processing around 2.5%–2.7% plus $0.10 and online processing around 2.9%–3.5% plus $0.30.
limitations: Claims statement-audit experience but does not publish the sample or methodology; the cited overall average overlaps other publishers' underlying statistic.

sourceRecords.title: Card Present vs. Card Not Present Transactions
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes card-not-present interchange around 2.25%–2.65%, about 0.55–0.60 percentage points above its card-present comparison, plus named online processor examples.
limitations: The average interchange figures are not linked to a named primary schedule and the page has no stable publication date.

sourceRecords.title: Average Cost of Credit Card Processing Fees
sourceRecords.metricType: merchant fee range by pricing model
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes tiered card-present pricing up to about 2.9%, non-present pricing around 3.5%, and flat-rate and interchange-plus alternatives.
limitations: General pricing-model guidance, not a sample of e-commerce merchants in RateReveal's selected annual-volume tier.

sourceRecords.title: High-Risk Merchant Account Fees: How Much You'll Pay in 2026
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: General high-risk discount-rate and chargeback-fee discussion
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes a general high-risk discount-rate range of 3.5%–6.5% plus fixed transaction fees, with separate chargeback-fee context.
limitations: Chargeback-mitigation vendor; the numeric range is general high-risk guidance and does not isolate card-present vape merchants.

sourceRecords.title: High-Risk Merchant Account: 2026 Fees, Providers & Approval
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: High-risk fee range, reserve context, and regulated-retail examples
sourceRecords.metricType: general high-risk fee range and reserve context
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Describes high-risk pricing around 2.5%–6.5%, rolling reserves around 5%–20%, and names vape or smoke shops as regulated retail.
limitations: POS vendor rather than a processor, and the numeric range is not separately measured for vape or CBD merchants.

sourceRecords.title: Navigating Merchant Processing for CBD Shops: Gateways and Beyond
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: States that legal hemp-derived CBD merchants typically see processing fees around 3.5%–5%, depending on volume, history, and online or in-store channel.
limitations: A CBD processor selling services and the only CBD-specific numeric source in the research pass; no independent corroboration was found.

sourceRecords.title: Your Guide to High-Risk Merchant Account Fees & Rates in 2026
sourceRecords.locationWithinSource: General high-risk processing rate and reserve discussion
sourceRecords.supportedObservation: Advertises general high-risk processing around 3.49%–3.95% and rolling reserves generally around 5%–10%, with higher reserves possible.
limitations: Processor-advertised pricing is not an observed market distribution, and repeated republication of this figure is not independent evidence.

entries.displayLabel: RateReveal full-service restaurant / bar reference range

synthesis.evidenceSummary: Restaurant-specific provider observations place competitive interchange-plus pricing near the lower end and flat-rate outcomes near the upper end, while broader card-present cost context and premium-card exposure explain meaningful variation.
synthesis.rateRevealRationale: RateReveal selected 1.80%–2.90% as a deliberately broad contextual range spanning the observed restaurant floor through plausible flat-rate outcomes for the approved profile; the endpoints are RateReveal product judgment, not externally certified boundaries.
assumptions: The merchant is U.S., standard risk, primarily card present, and processes approximately $100,000–$500,000 annually.
The range reflects overall processing price and does not normalize every merchant's card mix, ticket size, processor markup, or pricing structure.
limitations: No disclosed-methodology restaurant effective-rate population study was found.
Cuisine, debit share, rewards mix, average ticket, qualification outcomes, and statement-specific fees can materially change the result.
Approximate RateReveal reference range, not an official restaurant industry rate or guaranteed target.
Position against this range does not prove overcharging, breach, processor error, or recoverable savings.

entries.displayLabel: RateReveal grocery / specialty food reference range

synthesis.evidenceSummary: Primary network and regulator data establish lower supermarket and debit cost context, while grocery payment-mix research supports the importance of debit share. The evidence explains the range but does not observe a grocery merchant-rate population.
synthesis.rateRevealRationale: RateReveal selected 1.60%–2.60% to reflect favorable debit and supermarket economics at the low end and ordinary credit, rewards, markup, and qualification variability at the high end for the approved base profile.
assumptions: The merchant is U.S., standard risk, primarily card present, and processes approximately $100,000–$500,000 annually.
The merchant's activity and account coding are compatible with grocery or specialty-food treatment; regulated and exempt debit mix remains merchant-specific.
limitations: The synthesis is driven by interchange and debit economics rather than a statistical grocery effective-rate study.
Specialty merchants may not qualify for supermarket network programs, and regulatory debit rules require monitoring.
Approximate RateReveal reference range, not a network-mandated supermarket rate or guaranteed target.
Debit mix, MCC/program qualification, card rewards, ticket size, pricing structure, and processor fees can materially change the outcome.

entries.displayLabel: RateReveal general card-present retail reference range

synthesis.evidenceSummary: Several differently motivated sources converge on card-present and small-business pricing in the mid-two to mid-three percent range, with volume, card mix, and fee inclusion explaining dispersion.
synthesis.rateRevealRationale: RateReveal selected 2.50%–3.50% as the strongest broad standard-retail contextual range in this research pass, bounded to the approved card-present and $100,000–$500,000 profile and intentionally excluding high-risk retail.
assumptions: The merchant is U.S., standard risk, card present, and processes approximately $100,000–$500,000 annually.
The business is ordinary general retail rather than an approved high-risk, e-commerce, fuel, grocery, or other separately modeled segment.
limitations: The sources do not publish a disclosed statistical distribution for the exact volume tier.
Repeated general-industry rules of thumb were not treated as independent statistical observations.
RateReveal contextual reference only; not an official retail benchmark, processor term, or guaranteed target.
Do not apply to high-risk retail or merchants whose channel, volume, risk, or business activity materially differs.

synthesis.evidenceSummary: Multiple sources distinguish card-not-present from card-present economics and place interchange-plus or blended online pricing above comparable in-person pricing, with published contexts spanning roughly the low-two to mid-three percent area.
synthesis.rateRevealRationale: RateReveal selected 2.30%–3.20% to represent the approved standard-risk e-commerce profile without collapsing it into card-present retail; the narrower upper boundary reflects a contextual review range rather than worst-case flat-rate pricing.
assumptions: The merchant is U.S., standard risk, card not present, and processes approximately $100,000–$500,000 annually.
The statement's verified effective-rate basis is comparable and does not hide materially different populations or unsupported high-risk activity.
limitations: No source isolates a statistical e-commerce merchant distribution at the exact annual-volume tier.
Fraud, chargebacks, card mix, gateway fees, cross-border activity, pricing model, and ticket size can materially alter results.
RateReveal contextual reference only; not an official e-commerce industry rate or guaranteed target.
CNP economics are materially different from card-present retail, and this range must not be reused for other channels or risk profiles.

entries.displayLabel: RateReveal vape / approved high-risk retail reference range

synthesis.evidenceSummary: General high-risk sources support a broad 3.5%–6.5% pricing context and substantially higher reserve and chargeback exposure; the limited CBD- and vape-linked figures are commercially biased and not independent market samples.
synthesis.rateRevealRationale: RateReveal selected the intentionally broad 3.50%–6.50% range for confirmed, legitimate, supported high-risk card-present retail because risk economics are directionally strong while public segment-specific evidence remains thin.
assumptions: The merchant is a legitimate and supported U.S. high-risk retail business with confirmed activity, confirmed high-risk context, card-present processing, and approximately $100,000–$500,000 annual volume.
Reserves, chargeback fees, gateway costs, and settlement holds remain separate terms and are not automatically represented by the effective-rate comparison.
limitations: The evidence is thin, commercially biased, and lacks a disclosed vape-specific merchant-rate distribution.
Mixed or card-not-present high-risk processing, unsupported activity, or unconfirmed eligibility remains unavailable.
Approximate RateReveal reference for confirmed approved high-risk retail only; not a processor approval promise or official industry rate.
The range is broad and low confidence; position does not prove overcharging or create recoverable savings.
